changes.before: Open the built-in editor to change a file. The source notes that the code command requires Classic mode.
changes.after: Open the built-in editor from the toolbar or run code <filename> to edit a file.
changes.reason: Current editor documentation supports code directly and no longer specifies the training unit’s Classic-mode restriction.

changes.before: Cloud Shell is not intended for concurrent independent sessions across subscriptions or tenants.
changes.after: Cloud Shell has a default limit of 20 concurrent users per tenant; request a quota increase for larger training sessions.
changes.reason: Replace an unqualified concurrency limitation from training with the current documented tenant quota.

changes.before: Deploy the empty template and inspect its successful deployment record; it creates no resources until resources are declared.
changes.after: Deploy the empty template in the default incremental mode and inspect its successful deployment record; it creates no resources.
changes.reason: An empty complete-mode deployment can delete existing resources; identify the exercise’s default incremental mode.

changes.before: Redeploying after a parameter or template change applies the required resource updates rather than duplicating unchanged resources.
changes.after: Redeploying with the same resource names and scopes updates existing resources. In incremental mode, specify all non-default properties because omitted properties can reset to defaults.
changes.reason: Clarify resource identity and the important distinction between incremental resource deployment and property merging.

changes.before: The source recommends Entra Cloud Sync for most synchronization scenarios and reserves Connect Sync for more complex requirements.
changes.after: Cloud Sync uses lightweight agents with cloud-managed synchronization; choose Cloud Sync or Connect Sync after comparing the capabilities your deployment requires.
changes.reason: Current Cloud Sync product documentation includes device synchronization; avoid treating the training unit’s broad product recommendation as a fixed capability boundary.

changes.before: Dynamic membership requires the appropriate license; the source identifies Entra ID P1 and Intune for Education for applicable device rules.
changes.after: Dynamic user groups require enough Entra ID P1 or Intune for Education licenses for every unique user member; dynamic device group members need no license.
changes.reason: The training note incorrectly implies a device-membership license requirement and mislimits Intune for Education.

changes.before: The source recommends Cloud Kerberos Trust for new hybrid scenarios requiring on-premises single sign-on rather than device writeback.
changes.after: Windows Hello for Business cloud Kerberos trust enables on-premises authentication from Entra joined or hybrid joined devices after Microsoft Entra Kerberos and the required policies are configured.
changes.reason: Scope cloud Kerberos trust to Windows Hello for Business; current device-writeback documentation still describes distinct certificate-trust and AD FS scenarios.

changes.before: Supported attribute types include Boolean, integer and string, with single or multiple values and predefined or free-form choices.
changes.after: Attribute types are Boolean, integer and string. Integer and string attributes can allow multiple values or predefined choices; Boolean attributes are single-valued.
changes.reason: Product documentation excludes Boolean attributes from multiple values and predefined-value lists.

changes.before: A resource group contains resources; a resource belongs to one group at a time. Groups cannot be nested or renamed.
changes.after: A resource group contains resource-group-scoped resources; each belongs to one group at a time. Some resources, such as policy definitions, exist at subscription or management-group scope. Groups cannot be nested or renamed.
changes.reason: The training’s blanket resource-group membership statement overlooks subscription- and management-group-scoped resource types.

changes.before: Settings assigned at parent scopes are inherited by child scopes, including subscriptions and their resources.
changes.after: Azure RBAC assignments and Azure Policy assignments at parent scopes apply to child scopes, including subscriptions and their resources.
changes.reason: Settings do not universally inherit: use the precise access and policy constructs taught in this unit.

changes.before: Governance disciplines include cost management, security baseline, resource consistency, identity baseline and deployment acceleration.
changes.after: Governance policies cover regulatory compliance, security, operations, costs, data and resource management.
changes.reason: Use the current governance areas described in the same unit instead of presenting the older five-discipline model as the only current model.

changes.before: A deployIfNotExists assignment can use a managed identity for remediation; choose the required identity and permissions deliberately.
changes.after: Remediation for deployIfNotExists or modify requires a managed identity on the assignment with the necessary Azure RBAC permissions.
changes.reason: A managed identity is required for remediation, rather than an optional feature of deployIfNotExists.

changes.before: The reset process identifies the user, verifies identity using configured methods, accepts a new password and sends a notification.
changes.after: The reset process identifies the user, verifies identity using configured methods, accepts a new password and can send configured notifications.
changes.reason: User reset notifications are configurable, not unconditional.

changes.before: Configure notifications so users can notice an unexpected reset and administrators can be alerted to other administrator resets.
changes.after: Enable user notifications to reveal unexpected resets, and enable administrator notifications so Global Administrators are alerted when another administrator resets a password.
changes.reason: Current documentation identifies Global Administrators as recipients, rather than every administrator role.

changes.before: Check the required licenses for your users and deployment. Hybrid password writeback needs supported licensing and synchronization configuration.
changes.after: Cloud-only password reset requires an eligible Microsoft 365 or Entra premium license. On-premises password writeback requires Entra ID P1/P2 or Microsoft 365 Business Premium plus supported synchronization configuration.
changes.reason: Replace a vague licensing reminder with verified requirements; Business Standard alone does not permit writeback.

changes.before: Configure the required number of authentication methods and the allowed methods.
changes.after: Set the required number of methods in Password reset. Manage allowed methods in the Authentication methods policy; security questions remain in the SSPR policy.
changes.reason: Legacy MFA and SSPR method controls were deprecated from September 30, 2025; use the current policy while retaining the security-question exception.

changes.before: Review authentication methods, registration and notifications, and configure the helpdesk contact.
changes.after: Review the required method count, registration and notifications in Password reset, enable Email OTP for the pilot users in the Authentication methods policy, and configure the helpdesk contact.
changes.reason: Update the exercise’s legacy Email method configuration to the current authentication policy.

changes.before: Prepare the background and logo image files according to the official exercise’s format and size requirements.
changes.after: Use an eligible licensed tenant and an Organizational Branding Administrator, then prepare background and logo files to the current branding image requirements.
changes.reason: Include required licensing/role and use current image requirements rather than relying on old exercise sizing.
